notes.title: Crusher's Briefing: Chronodeck Update 1.2
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/4e62414bd612cfb4b5e8fe312b1b826cd22f29e7.png[/img]

Agents,

This is Crusher. Listen up. The Chronodeck Update 1.2 has dropped, bringing powerful new assets and crucial intel straight from the frontlines.

We aim to test your performance on high-skill-level challenges and compare it with that of other agents worldwide.

[h1]What's new?[/h1]

"📢" [i]marks the changes suggested by the Deadlink community[/i]

[h1]The Chronodeck[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/2e7933aca71b03040fdf95c627ec6526f9f3c458.gif[/img]

Introducing The Chronodeck, CSA’s brand-new game mode! In this variant, you'll face three special time trial maps for each Combat Shell, giving you 12 unique challenges. On each map, you'll need to collect coins and defeat enemies within a tight time limit. If you can beat certain times, you'll earn medals that are displayed on global leaderboards, so you can see how you stack up against other players. Plus, by securing the best medals, you'll unlock exclusive weapon skins.

[b]The Chronodeck mode becomes available upon destroying the Torantula spider tank at least four times.[/b]

[h2]📢 Now on Consoles[/h2]
Good news for our console operators — Deadlink is releasing shortly on the blue and green platforms. Experience the latest Chronodeck Update and all its features on [url=https://store.playstation.com/concept/10010769]PlayStation[/url] and [url=https://www.xbox.com/games/store/deadlink/9mx7952w6psq]Xbox[/url]. Get it loaded, prepare for deployment, and check out the Chronodeck [url=https://x.com/CrunchingKoalas/status/1818007581203333331]records contest[/url].

[h2]📢 Community-Inspired Implants[/h2]
Remember the “design your own implant” contest we had a while ago? Guess what, the winning ideas are now implemented into the game. Congratulations to the winners once more! Try out the Oppenheimer Gauntlets, Excess Heat Dissipator, Allied Summoners, and seven more new ways to be the killing machine you always dreamed of.

[h2]Official Deadlink Wiki[/h2]
Thanks to the invaluable work of [b]ZUltra3166[/b], the official, community-driven Deadlink wiki is now live and up-to-date on the wiki.gg platform. Curious about the crit damage of the Rocket Launcher at Lv.3? Yeah, you can even get that kind of info there!

[url=https://deadlink.wiki.gg/]Official Deadlink Wiki by ZUltra3166[/url]

[h2]Other Changes[/h2]
[list]
[*] 📢 Lots of gamepad improvements
[*] 📢 Interact and Melee key binds are now separate
[*] Added a wiki link to the main menu
[*] 📢 Improved the performance of the Extant Existence mode
[*] Added full localization for the Ukrainian language
[*] Balance changes for a smoother experience on lower difficulty levels
[*] Minor fixes and optimization improvements
[/list]
[h3]Special Offer: Daily Deal Reminder[/h3]
Heads up, new recruits and those waiting on the sidelines: the Daily Deal is live, but it’s not going to last forever. The deadline is August 3rd. This is your shot to join the ranks at a reduced cost. Don’t miss it — get in the game before it’s too late.

[h3]Join Our Community![/h3]
We encourage all agents, new and veteran, to share your experiences and strategies from the Chronodeck Update in our [url=https://discord.gg/5jJEBfCd]Discord server[/url]. It's the perfect place to connect, discuss tactics, and get the latest updates straight from HQ.

[i]Stay vigilant,
Crusher
CSA, and proud to serve[/i]

notes.title: 🚀 Design Implant & Win Prizes Contest Winners Announced!
notes.content:
Agents of Deadlink, the moment we've all been eagerly awaiting has arrived! After an incredible display of creativity and ingenuity, we're thrilled to announce the winners of the "Design Implant & Win Prizes" contest. Your submissions were nothing short of spectacular, bringing new depths of innovation to the Deadlink universe.

[h3]🌟 Delving into Your Designs: A Fun Journey[/h3]
Going through each and every reported implant was not just insightful; it was an absolute joy! You revealed the creativity and diversity of ideas, making our task both enjoyable and exciting. It's been a fun-filled journey, exploring the myriad ways you envision enhancing the Deadlink gameplay.

And the Winners are...

[h2]🥇 1st Place[/h2]
[h3]Vern Carson - Oppenheimer Gauntlets[/h3]
[code]Active Effects:
Level 1: Melee attacks cause an AOE explosion in a 1m radius for 6s, dealing 75% melee damage.
Level 2: Melee attacks cause an AOE explosion in a 2m radius for 7s, dealing 100% melee damage.
Level 3: Melee attacks cause an AOE explosion in a 3m radius for 8s, dealing 125% melee damage.
Level 4: Melee attacks cause an AOE explosion in a 4m radius for 8s, dealing 150% melee damage. 
Enemies killed by the explosion detonate, dealing 50% melee damage in a 4m radius.

Passive Effects:
Level 1: Meleeing an enemy has a 5% chance to ignite them.
Level 2: Meleeing an enemy has a 10% chance to ignite them.
Level 3: Meleeing an enemy has a 15% chance to ignite them.
Level 4: Meleeing an enemy has a 15% chance to ignite them. 
Killing an ignited enemy with melee damage will spread Ignite to enemies in a 4m radius.[/code]
[h2]🥈 2nd Place[/h2]
[h3]Sabet - Excess Heat Dissipator[/h3]
[code]Active Effects:
Level 1: Next dash will trigger an explosion that deals 5% of current skill damage.
Level 2: Next dash will trigger an explosion that deals 10% of current skill damage.
Level 3: Next dash will trigger an explosion that deals 20% of current skill damage.
Level 4: Next dash will trigger an explosion that deals 30% of current skill damage and pushes away everyone in the explosion radius.

Passive Effects:
Level 1-3: Dash will recharge 10% slower.
Level 4: Dash will recharge 15% slower. For each enemy in the explosion radius, recharge 25% dash.[/code]
[h2]🥉 3rd Place[/h2]
[h3]Masus - Allied Summoners*[/h3]
[code]Active Effects:
Level 1: Summons a drone that fights alongside the player.
Level 2: Summons a drone capable of inflicting poison damage.
Level 3: Summons two drones, both capable of inflicting poison damage.
Level 4: Summons two drones capable of inflicting poison damage and stunning an enemy every 10 seconds.
Note: Drones, once destroyed, will not respawn until the level is finished.

Passive Effects:
Level 1: For every kill a drone achieves, the player gains +5 temporary shields.[/code]
[h3]🏅 Prizes[/h3]
Congratulations to our winners, who will receive their respective prizes, including the Xtrfy Mouse, Deadlink Poster, and Deadlink Game Steam Key. We also extend a heartfelt thank you to all participants for your incredible contributions. 

[h3]🎄 Season's Greetings[/h3]
As we celebrate the success of this contest, we'd also like to extend warm holiday wishes to you all. May this festive season bring joy, peace, and further creativity to you and your loved ones. Here's to a wonderful holiday season and an exciting New Year filled with more adventures in the ever-expanding universe of videogames!

Thank you, Agents, for making this contest a wonderfully fun and memorable event. 
Merry Christmas and Happy Holidays! 🔥🎅🏼🎉

[i]Gruby Entertainment Team[/i]

notes.content:

We're thrilled to introduce a brand new feature in this Deadlink update, one that many of our dedicated players have been clamoring for: Extant Existence, also known as Endless Mode!

Alongside the addition of a new game mode, Deadlink has also received a significant round of balance tweaks and bug fixes to enhance overall gameplay stability and fairness.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/c8ab7b8e700d090b96a05e8e37eb75dedd67b59e.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/cb31dc54b0b69b6a8ca990523920125bb2f64d77.png[/img]
Endless Mode was a highly requested addition from our passionate player community, offering an opportunity to truly put your skills to the test or simply enjoy infinite gameplay for relaxation.

Dive into the simulation in a brand-new special area where waves of enemies will spawn one after another, challenging your survival instincts and combat skills. As you face your enemies, you'll be rewarded for your skills with implants and upgrades, becoming stronger and even more badass with each victorious encounter.

Endless Mode serves a dual purpose: a thrilling challenge to see how long you can endure the relentless onslaught and a perfect training ground to experiment with weapon combinations and implant synergies.

So, gear up, sharpen your reflexes, and step into the endless simulation of Extant Existence. How long can you survive? How powerful can you become? The answers await in Deadlink's most exhilarating update yet!

[b]Endless Mode becomes available upon reaching the Femto corporation and also introduces:[/b]
[list]
[*] 1 new skin for each primary weapon
[*] 4 new achievements

Ever-increasing profits and efficiency led Interport to [b]appoint an AI as CEO[/b]. AIs aren’t new for corporations, [b]advising countless[/b] cutthroat decisions and market strategies, but this was quite bold.

Interport’s limitless resources created an [b]engineering marvel[/b], built with [b]trinary logic[/b], a Soviet concept unexplored since the domination of binary computing. Iskra is a massive foe with a massive ego and a massive arsenal. While its divinity complex might be a delusion, it is truly a master of saturating its environment with death. 

Your greatest challenge in this fight will be to avoid Iskra's attacks. Always stay aware of your surroundings! notes.content:
What do you get when a ruthless PMC works together with an unscrupulous biotech corporation to create a supersoldier? You get our next boss - the Phoenix Apex.

The top of the line, the cream of the crop. The [b]most elite[/b] member of the Phoenix force, augmented with experimental military-grade cybernetics infused with the toughest nanolattice alloys money can buy.

Uplifted with [b]Watts-Rucker's gene therapy[/b]. More wetware than the average Phoenix soldier, but definitely [b]less Homo Sapiens, more Homo Patent[/b] at this point. Created for solely one purpose: stopping the menace plaguing Watts-Rucker operations. The corporate dealings leading to its creation must be the stuff of lawyering legend.
[/code]
The Phoenix Apex is a melee powerhouse that would love nothing more than to get up close and personal with your Combat Shell. What's left of you as a result might just fit into a Watts-Rucker test tube. 

That's why maintaining distance is key. Remember to use the C-Balls to your advantage. They'll aid you not only with resources, but with traversal opportunities to help you stay ahead in the fight against the Apex. 

Keep a close eye on its shield as well. When it's up, the Phoenix Apex is fully protected and able to throw back just about everything you throw at it. Time your attacks and pick the right angle to strike at this brute or wait for Mothership to spawn its drones and hit them all with a grenade - this will create a fountain of shields.

notes.title: Combat Shell Deep Dive #4 - Juggernaut
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/452ace16c71122de595f9ab7b0d68b8959469043.png[/img]

In the chronicles of Deadlink's unending combats against ruthless corporations, our previous explorations have taken us deep into the Combat Shells – from the agile [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1676130/view/3651904437094599342]Soldier[/url] and the battle-hardened [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1676130/view/3665415870861450102]Hunter[/url], to the ingenious [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1676130/view/3665415870887771278]Engineer[/url]. These insights have peeled back the layers of strategy and strength that define each shell.

But as the tides of corporate brutality continue to surge, a fresh gust of innovation arrives with the Full Release update – Juggernaut Combat Shell. Stepping onto the battlefield under the endorsement of the CSA and birthed by the audacious minds at CORE, Juggernaut comes throwing a whole lot of flak at your enemies while bending physics for [strike]fun and profit[/strike] offense and defense.

The [b]fourth[/b] sanctioned CSA Combat Shell, made to [b]deal with nano-augmented opponents[/b]. The Juggernaut Combat Shell is a mix of heavy industry and [b]open sourced[/b] components tying together the limits of strength, armor, deceptive speed, and low budget.

Some CSA funds requisitioned from corporations are spent on [b]deepening connections[/b] with the CORE [b]makerverse[/b], punks, and anti-authoritarians. This relationship built on mutual corporate hatred allowed the creation of a new class of shell, the holdout sent to finish the job against corruption. Work with tinkerers and open-source nutjobs allowed the CSA to think outside of the box, integrating [b]slipspace technology[/b] in new unique ways. Its speed is unmatched for its armor and size, allowing the use of a [b]heavy scattergun loadout[/b].
[/code]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/56f0f5ccd6df6637b89d453e11dfee16c50c5498.png[/img]

From a mean bruiser packing a heavy shield, the Juggernaut went on to develop into something a lot more experimental, deflecting bullets not with slabs of alloy, but with theoretical physics!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/2443cc2126c08d8f1a3840742c11a0a6487545cf.gif[/img]
The [b]Stray Redirector[/b] reroutes incoming blasts through slipspace, making the already armored Combat Shell outright invulnerable. Though wherever those blasts are getting rerouted just might mean someone somewhere is going to have a very bad day. 

The Combat Shell remains quite punchy as well, specifically with [b]Graviton Punch[/b] both bringing the heat and providing for some striking bursts of speed.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/d30d2b8416c783b660755cc90756706b944331cb.png[/img]

While Juggernaut's abilities pack a punch, the weapons have a bit of a kick to them. Rounding off the Combat Shell's arsenal is the beast of a sawed-off shotgun known as [b]Primed Eliminator[/b] and the open-sourced GNU+Cluster launcher firing grenades that explode into a front-facing arc of deadly shrapnel. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/5f24cb03a9651c532f1762235a94905c5e4b45bf.png[/img]

Did you trust the collab between CSA and the makerverse? Did you become a fan of it? With all four Combat Shells unleashed, let us know if the Juggernaut made its mark!

Some CSA funds requisitioned from corporations are spent on [b]deepening connections[/b] with the CORE [b]makerverse[/b], punks, and anti-authoritarians. This relationship built on mutual corporate hatred allowed the creation of a new class of shell, the holdout sent to finish the job against corruption. Work with tinkerers and open-source nutjobs allowed the CSA to think outside of the box, integrating [b]slipspace technology[/b] in new unique ways. Its speed is unmatched for its armor and size, allowing the use of a [b]heavy scattergun loadout[/b].
[/code]
[h2]Juggernaut’s Abilities[/h2]

[h3]Graviton Punch[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/70398e51ebd1cb12bf2f2e256d1c4290d95af58d.gif[/img]

A high-velocity kinetic impact coming from your fists, it launches the Combat Shell in the direction of the crosshair. Stuns enemies.

[h3]Stray Redirector[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/6e751577160a0802dd6315f3b20c2b29721e98d7.gif[/img]

Defensive mode, absorbs incoming damage whilst maintaining mobility. On ability reactivation or after a fixed period it explodes outward, dealing damage and marking nearby enemies.

[h2]New Arsenal[/h2]

[h3]Prime Eliminator[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/03101d95cae9a4ea81c5cd8ebd3685f32962cd7c.gif[/img]

A sawed-off shotgun of ungodly and unseemly power. The recoil alone will knock a Combat Shell back. Every trigger pull results in two shots, on press and release.

[h3]GNU+Cluster[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/433a322fda8016eebc5e47e6909cbc89c95fc148.gif[/img]

A cannon shooting a 40mm grenade that explodes mid-air, throwing shrapnel in a frontal arc.

[h3]SMRT Coil[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/d4b654f1fd23e0f5f9e534ca00128cbfa47834ba.gif[/img]

A coil creating short-range arcs, dealing electric damage in front of the user.

[h3]Blaze Mode[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/faf6187f6ae3fe03510958bf100cf0617dba4186.gif[/img]

A short-range jet burner dealing fire damage, its damage output increasing with proximity to the target.

[h3]Goob Launcher[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/9b3b96ce70947cc4264d3b1755ee46e469d4190a.gif[/img]

An industrial-grade toxic goob launcher. Damages enemies over time, hindering their movement. Goobjectiles stick to horizontal surfaces.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/c8ab7b8e700d090b96a05e8e37eb75dedd67b59e.png[/img]
[h2]Also new in Deadlink[/h2]

[h3]New Implants[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/b03c54167ea0cac450ba5c5de16c6ec95f0a388b.png[/img]

11 brand-new implants are available during runs.

[h3]The Plot Thickens[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/2b9d09920295ad4c8b6f89c847bb8e17ae86d9a4.gif[/img]

Dive into new captivating story elements that delve into the Agent’s work for the CSA, revealing intriguing revelations about their true identity.

[h3]Chatters and Voice-overs[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/2032d157303f2a1d0bd6b7ba26543ddfb82192d4.png[/img]

Experience the ultimate immersion, featuring mesmerizing voice-overs and a chatter system that brings your runs to life, fully immersing you in the thrilling world of the Deadlink megacorporations.

[h3]HUB Upgrades Rework[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/00194226703956ae00dc3b77f81478c5c31ccfdf.png[/img]

The HUB upgrade tree is no longer a work in progress. We analyzed tons of runs done by streamers and our Discord community. Some of the upgrades got removed, others reworked, and, of course, some of them are completely new.

[h3]📢 Rutger’s Casino[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/aa2cf07fb319d2d703843f4efc3d70d013247cbc.gif[/img]

Rutger needed some love; we all know that. But here's the thing: if you dig through trash piles, you'll discover more than just implants. Prepare for an epic journey, delving into the world of scrap in a quest to find useful (or maybe not so useful) treasures. And guess what? With the ever-increasing inflation, XPs have become an absolute must for running a thriving trash business.

[h3]📢 Weapon Inspect Animations[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/7aab5e61588241b7594bffd228044d1192d8d65b.gif[/img]

We saw that you really like the new animations, and honestly, we love them too! That’s why we added more. You can now also play the inspect animation directly using the [b]X[/b] key by default.

[h2]New Steam stuff[/h2]

[h3]Achievements[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/70a022d14b44da9d308b1c9717a4ff2d1b1a9694.png[/img]

You asked for them; you got them. Some of them are hard, like really hard. But that’s why they’re called achievements, right?

[h3]Localization[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/d29e0d2baa2f6cc7132e587ce137b33b89f4878b.png[/img]

Die Toten Link ++ Lien Mort ++ 死链接 ++ Enlace Muerto ++ デッドリンク ++ Ölü Bağlantı ++ Martwe Łącze ++ Мертвая Cсылка

[h3]Steam Cards (soon™)[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/2d3acf2a2f069482a8d9a2b9b85bf78137ddfc55.png[/img]

It’s [b]not[/b] Magic: The Gathering, but on the other hand, you can collect `em all!

[h2]Balance Changes[/h2]

[h3]Armor calculation[/h3]
The armor has been completely overhauled. Instead of acting as a second health bar and one-shot gating, now it is reducing incoming damage. The more armor, the more damage reduction. On top of that, every elemental damage will provide some armor-stripping capabilities, although the most efficient way to do so is still with Toxic/Corrosive damage type.

[h3]📢 Difficulty[/h3]
With the new armor system in mind, we have made adjustments to its values across higher difficulties. This change is aimed at encouraging our Agents to be more thoughtful in their choices of Implants and weapons. Addressing the concerns raised by hardcore players who found Neuromancy too easy, we have enhanced the challenge by making enemies stronger, with increased shooting speed and quicker reactions.

However, we haven't overlooked our non-hardcore players who simply want to enjoy the game. To provide a smoother experience, VR-Orientation will now feature less spongy enemies and reduced armor in later biomes. This way, you can freely experiment with different builds before taking on the challenges of Deep Dive and Neuromancy.

Furthermore, we have made slight adjustments to the XP gain from door rewards, allowing you to obtain your upgrades a bit sooner. We hope these changes will enhance your overall gaming experience.

[h3]Neuralboosts[/h3]
Neuralboost reward got shifted to the regular reward pool, so it's not handed out before every implant selection anymore. This is a big balance tweak for the build's power consistency. Now players can decide whether they want to boost their combat stats vertically or broaden their progress by adding a new shell and weapon upgrades horizontally.

[h3]📢 Soldier’s Shotgun[/h3]
[list]
[*] Number of pellets decreased ([b]20 ➡️ 10[/b])
[*] Shotgun damage increased ([b]5 ➡️ 12[/b])
[*] Detection radius for shotgun pellets increased, and the detection radius curve changed to be less aggressive (projectiles will have a bigger detection radius of up to 20 meters). This should improve the shotgun feel and damage delivery.
[*] Reload and Fire Rate Shotgun’s mods properties increased to make them a sensible alternative to other Shotgun mods.[/list]
[h3]Heavy Weapons’ Stats[/h3]
We noticed a major disproportion in terms of Heavy Weapon damage outcome. This change equalizes each of the secondary weapons to be as viable to play as any other.

However, this means that the EA saves won't sync with the current version, leading to a reset of progress on the affected save slot. To compensate for any inconvenience, you will receive a partial refund of XP and Turing Tokens. Get ready for an enhanced gaming experience, and thank you for being part of our journey!

notes.title: Combat Shell Deep Dive #3 - Engineer
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/637ffc4529266586ca054b84641958c0ef4b9b83.png[/img]

We approach our third Combat Shell Deep Dive and it's time to talk about the CSA's venerable field hacker frame. That is, of course, the Engineer submitted as a blueprint by hacker turned CSA Electronic Intelligence Expert, Maria Argentea.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/9bdc03cd489c9e7b0f445e6d43023b245ca8a774.png[/img]
The Engineer represents a middle ground between firepower and sigint. Its abilities are aimed at zone control and tactical area denial. Prominently visible on the Shell is the sting of its [b]Wormlink Breach[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/68f0c977b45cc44a17d0fb5ba7696f3d4dfce23e.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/906e9fd690249befba44d0635db3f9bf07684c60.png[/img]
Through this direct link the Engineer hacks cybernetics and electronics, using the cable as a conduit to deliver a software payload incapacitating enemies.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/93e07279a6733ab0441bbcbd98ca2777ac6267fd.gif[/img]
Key to its area denial capabilities is the [b]Lawbringer Turret[/b]. While its battery life is limited, it's chock full of sensors and IFF subroutines and has room for additional elemental mods for some deadly force multiplication. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/5bf4218cae477edb53021f40ebf4d428e60a2f76.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/f792e6fffb41a83a0d1366b264627f9864e5848c.png[/img]
As with other Shells, the Engineer hardly wades into battle emptyhanded. Your armaments, should you pick this Shell, are comprised of the flechette-firing [b]Gauss Rifle[/b] that combines respectable fire rate with good recoil control, and the [b]Tarball Grenade Launcher[/b] packed with sticky bombs by default.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/6fcf1745fa7545c773cccbd8dda51dfcaa4636b8.png[/img]
So how do you like Maria Argentea's gift, agents? Is it your favorite, or do you think the talented hacker just went for a blatant self-insert into the Protocol? Share your destructive Engineering experience in the comments below!

notes.title: Combat Shell Deep Dive #2 - Hunter
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/ae721f87aec81389051a49054c885f28a1cfd108.png[/img]
In Deadlink Protocol CSA and, by extension, you operate a variety of Combat Shells from the tried and true to risky and experimental. Today's deep dive is about the Hunter.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/f03589a44385981f74c431254556410c5f3a8997.gif[/img]
Stealthy, deadly, more precise and refined - those were the words Rumiko Usagi used to describe the Hunter when first pitching it. This Combat Shell represents an option for those operatives looking for more finesse in their operations.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/80ea971191c0c51fd5ff97d53d07a437db05b703.gif[/img]
Don't let the light armor of the Hunter deceive you - both weapons it's armed with pack a significant punch. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/8c8665f3b93478fb7a86c6a14330bd996693b5d6.png[/img]

The [b]Tora Peacekeeper[/b] variable-caliber hand-cannon makes up the Hunter's primary weapon, ideal for landing precise headshots. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/35b04c3ee2255ceff5776641a09a1d63cf1a49f6.gif[/img]
The Hunter's secondary weapon is an unorthodox energy weapon prototype, the [b]ARC Cannon[/b], generating a wide scalar arc that hits multiple enemies. Through elemental mods, it can also be transformed into a laser, particle accelerator or weaponized matter converter.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/410954e82bb001fcde1f426c8b989a0efed15460.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/1aae53aff17fe9d78d9d416fea68c76d04c7438e.gif[/img]
The Hunter is the lightest Combat Shell in terms of armor, which means it relies on mobility and deception to survive and maximize enemy casualties. One of its tools used to this end is the experimental [b]Switchback Translocator[/b], swapping places with a target and applying a mark to it in the process. The other is the [b]IFF Decoy[/b] that simultaneously projects a false image of the Hunter while also cloaking the actual Shell with an optical camouflage. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/bab4c846de4014d825cff35ea04e276961d3cb85.png[/img]
Have you made good use of the Hunter on your mission, agents? Did you master its armaments, or did you end up preferring one of the more robust Shells? Let us know about your Hunting experience. We are looking forward to hearing from you in the comments!

notes.title: Combat Shell Deep Dive #1 - Soldier
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/cc208eee18dbe3a41e0c3a6fcdbb28a8e2b2713f.png[/img]

In the Deadlink Protocol you are the brain but your variable brawn are the Combat Shells you connect to. Humanoid frames of armor, servos and circuits piloted by a copy of your consciousness into the thick of the fight against corporate greed. 

We are sure you would like to know your arsenal, and so it's time to take a deep dive into one of the combat shells at your disposal. This will include a summary of their arsenal, and a look at some behind-the-scenes WIPs that they evolved from into their current place in Deadlink!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/3179c4fcbf287a1b0a3093967b3cf09b150d6a8b.jpg[/img]
The [b]Soldier Combat Shell[/b] was among the first developed (both in-universe and out of it!), but don't mistake it for a grunt. This shell fits a combat specialist like a glove and is a tried and true tool of destruction. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/856acbf28443e2433d3b7c2581568fa146c6e824.jpg[/img]
Fittingly, it is armed with weapons just as firmly associated with destruction: a [b]shotgun[/b] and a [b]variable rocket launcher[/b]. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/75b0999599f22a7a6bc1da41c68770b8b3a7ec10.gif[/img]
Aiding in its mobility and adding control to range of engagement is the [b]GripWire Rappel[/b]. This PMC-grade nanotech grappling hook does more than just close the distance - it stuns opponents and tags them. Constructor Balls are just as valid a target for this useful tool.

Furthermore, the Soldier packs a highly disruptive punch in the form of the [b]Scrambler[/b]. This EMP-like attack will produce a cone of superfine magnetic particles, leaving opponents marked and, in most cases, incapacitated.

The Soldier Combat Shell may be your first tool, but it's certainly one with a lot of use and potential for mayhem. 

⠀⠀    [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/f7bf39f42ca01e3e12b363d58e8a39be0b0e2923.png[/img]
How did it feel to pilot the Soldier, agent? Did you stick to your tried and true guns for long, or quickly find yourself seeking out more specialized tools offered by the other Combat Shells? Share your comments and battle experience in the comments!

notes.title: Friends In Odd Places update
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/818a48c305b9ca93228c8270c84232ac801cb14d.jpg[/img]

The megacorps may want you to think the whole world is nothing but corporate mooks, but that is a lie. Sadly, nor is everyone a top class specialist in the employ of a cutting edge federal agency. In this minor update we are adding more characters that will expand the world of Deadlink and serve as some faces from outside CSA who you don’t have to hold at gunpoint. You will be able to meet them in the passageways leading from one combat room to the next. 

Read on to find out all about them and other changes in Deadlink!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/c8ab7b8e700d090b96a05e8e37eb75dedd67b59e.png[/img]
[h1]What’s new?[/h1]

"📢" [i]marks the changes suggested by the Deadlink community[/i]

[h2]From the streets...[/h2]

They may not be the first people you’d consider an alliance with, but hear them out. In the neon-lit future these independent thinkers have worked out a niche for themselves. Even the poor and downtrodden can afford to add some metal to their bodies. And seeing as you could always use new metal for your bodies, the expertise of these two might prove unexpectedly useful.

[h3]Chuck (The Maker)[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/f50ecbd6c0868d34091abc488047c4477c96f965.png[/img]

Take a 3D printing enthusiast. Now give him possibilities that match his enthusiasm. All that he owns he makes by himself, be it food or somewhat amateurish biohacked implants. Still, that's the price to pay to live on the outskirt of the general corporate society. These days this tinkerer and lifehacker is dedicated to the hobby of producing counterfeit matter with cracked C-Balls. Despite C-Ball lockdown procedures introduced in order to stop the likes of him from causing a grey goo event, he finds a way to make use of them and will help you reap some of the benefits.

[h3]Rutger (The Collector)[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/d1a831c80f528e9ac2c041c1b632887938265aa1.png[/img]

"Cyberhobo" isn't a very flattering name. He prefers Collector, vintage tech enthusiast at the point of being a tech pariah, unable to integrate with “modern” society. His insistence that newer doesn’t mean better dooms him to live a life disconnected from most existing comforts. Corporate anti-consumer practices make it impossible for you to log into the net without only the latest hardware and software, (regardless of the worsening user experience, missing features or blatant invasion of user privacy). Thus the Collector is without a bank account, a job or even an ability to buy groceries at most chains. He roams the streets of the CORE, looking for discarded tech, disassembling it for his own needs and sometimes reselling jailbroken computers, implants and phones to likeminded, yet more fortunate individuals. Sometimes he finds an odd modern implant that’s useless to him that he’ll happily gift to you.

[h2]... And from corporate confines[/h2]

These two may be employed by Watts, but are not on CSA’s target list. That said, either one would love for you to target the other. Talk about a lab rivalry gone sour. Hear them out and see what you can obtain from these brilliant minds locked in conflict. 

[h3]Irène & Carl (The Rivals)[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/a254ca4df96e827dc9219f6a94b98a0cc88a0a41.png[/img]

Both are geniuses in the fields of gene splicing, protein design and piezoelectric interfaces, their work bringing millions to the company, and the small trickle of knowledge making it into scientific journals deemed as nothing but revolutionary. Doesn’t stop them from being petty and sabotaging each other’s research. Neither one seems especially concerned about the long term ramifications of trusting an outside party to destroy the property of the very corporation that pays them.

[h2]📢 Heavy Weapons Leveling and Rarities[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/0447d3260a28832b732ec2ab996dbe08372d5753.png[/img]

Gun enthusiasts, rejoice! We heard your feedback, and we've implemented a new feature that takes heavy weapons to the next level, literally. With the leveling and rarities of heavy weapons, your arsenal just got a whole lot more powerful.

Our team has been paying close attention to the community's ideas and feedback about the weapons in the game. We drew a lot of conclusions and came up with a new system that we think you'll love. Each heavy weapon can now be leveled up to the max [b]level 4[/b]. As you level up your weapon, you'll gain stat boosts, making it even more lethal in battle.

But that's not all. Each heavy weapon can also be of [b]Common[/b], [b]Rare[/b], or [b]Legendary[/b] rarity. The Rare and Legendary weapons come with special affixes that significantly improve their viability in combat. These weapons are truly one of a kind and will give you a real edge on the battlefield.

When you receive a heavy weapon as a reward, you'll be presented with a choice. You can [b]either[/b] level up your current secondary weapon or swap to one of two different, already leveled-up weapons. The choice is yours, and it'll help you customize your arsenal to suit your playstyle.

Please note that this system is still evolving, and we may change it in the future. But for now, we're excited to see how our community will use this new feature to dominate their opponents. Level up your heavy weapons, increase their rarity, and become a true force to be reckoned with.

[h2]Implants[/h2]
[list]
[*] Airburst Catalyst, Ora Empathy Inhibitor, and Myoactuator Enhancer stacks will persist between biomes
[*] Units changed to meters in implant descriptions and Deadlink upgrades
[*] Static Inference Generator - fixed leveling description, fixed Shock not taking effect on multiple enemies
[*] Thermite Cartridge Coating - changed passive from "Extra 25 Fire Damage on both weapons" to "Both weapons have 25% chance to Ignite enemies hit"
[*] Tooltip window updated to the new card view

[*] Implants are locked by default and must be found during the run to get their preview in the Codex Library
[*] Implants sold in the shop will no longer appear on implant level-up selection
[/list]
[h2]Defibrillator[/h2]
This Deadlink upgrade proved to be more problematic than we thought. This is why it got a complete overhaul. The Defibrillator upgrade will now:
[list]
[*] Clamp the player’s HP to 1
[*] Refresh all ability cooldowns
[*] Refill ammo in both weapons
[*] Grant complete damage immunity for a short duration
[*] Work only once per run
[/list]
[h2]📢 Trinary Iskra iteration[/h2]
[list]

[*] Added various laser patterns for Stage 4
[/list]
[h2]Other Changes[/h2]

[*] 📢 Prevented duplicates in the Starting Pack selection

[*] Additional improvements for gamepad handling. Deadlink now has Full controller support.
[*] Electric Grenade description now matches its mechanic.

[*] Added enemy stun effect diminishing returns, so it won’t be that easy to stunlock enemies anymore
[*] Intel XeSS version updated to 1.2.6

[/list]

Laws can't keep up with regulating the latest biochemical stimulants, the cops don't even know what counts as a cybercrime this week and the inertia of the bureaucratic machine is no match to the sleek, agile, AI-assisted decision-making of the latest zaibatsu front. The agency plays by corporate rules. notes.title: The Interport update is here!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/fe6a04a57d837857d51bf80468072b5fff95748e.jpg[/img]

The wait is over. Time to bust down the doors of a new corporation, agents! 

In this [b]major update[/b] you'll be able to start raiding Interport, a global e-commerce giant. Read on to find out more about Interport and the enemies that it's going to throw at you, as well as implant leveling, implant rarity, challenge rooms, balance adjustments, changes, and more!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/c8ab7b8e700d090b96a05e8e37eb75dedd67b59e.png[/img]
[h1]What’s new?[/h1]

"📢" [i]marks the changes suggested by the Deadlink community[/i]

[h2]Pay a visit to Interport[/h2]

[code][table noborder=1 equalcells=1]
    [tr]
        [th]Name[/th]
        [th]Category[/th]
        [th]ID[/th]
    [/tr]
    [tr]
        [td]INTERPORT[/td]
        [td]ONLINE RETAILER[/td]
        [td]INN0231351067[/td]
    [/tr]
[/table]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/0eb31ce886979168d7e08fd0224894f653074aee.png[/img]

Interport (short for [b]Internet-Eksport[/b], Rus. интернет-экспорт) traces its origins back to late-stage USSR, starting as a [b]humble co-operative store in Moscow[/b]. While the original perestroikan law was written to allow worker-owned businesses, Interport was started by a crafty politburo member who wanted a financial life raft for the fall of the USSR. 

With the initial injection of future [b]oligarch money[/b], Interport quickly privatized factories and dominated the market with cheap goods the impoverished populace could afford. The company concentrated on [b]cutting costs[/b], repurposing steelworks as warehouses, and relocating food production to nickel refineries, worker and consumer [b]safety be damned[/b]. While the company established multiple supermarkets in the United States, it was their novel [b]online business[/b] that gained them a foothold and catapulted Interport on the trajectory that it is on to this day.

Over the years, Interport became the [b]world's go-to place for online purchases[/b]. Their operations on US soil became [b]huge warehouses[/b], cheaply and shoddily built to resemble the brutalist soviet factories as part of its pedigree, but with no intention of lasting longer than a few years. With such cost-reducing measures, the company has been [b]increasing its income[/b] exponentially.

In recent years, the focus on productivity led to Interport [b]appointing an AI as its CEO[/b] – a world first. Capable of making strategic decisions within nanoseconds, the incomprehensibly vast computer mind has introduced a requirement for all its administrative employees to [b]upload their consciousness[/b] into its decentralized network, effectively uplifting them to a [b]posthuman[/b] state of [b]maximum productivity[/b]. Just like subdermal chips and mandatory thought interceptor implants before, this was met with great enthusiasm by shareholders, as [b]workers ceded their bodies to the company[/b]. These mindless husks, augmented with industry-grade cybernetic enhancements to become [b]“biorobots”[/b], were sent to the factories and warehouses to [b]replace the baseline human and robot workforce[/b], effectively cutting costs of factory operations by 5.7%, leaving many economies in shambles.
[/code]
[h2]New Corporation To Raid[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/7c8f009b14c1de70a19d50d6a6472cefe84c7eca.gif[/img]

Experience the perilous consequences of unchecked corporate power as you battle against Interport's ruthless biorobot workforce in these dangerous arenas. Can you survive the ultimate showdown against the world's most powerful online retailer?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/63b7f7a5c2d6ca2deeee97d49d82163b59ce2413.gif[/img]

Be ready to face tough challenges as you fight against the dangerous forces of the Interport Corporation on their own treacherous turf. The gameplay will test your skills and strategy like never before, but the rewards for victory are worth the risk.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/0e06307d47fba88d499ec073dee328309173288d.gif[/img]

[h2]New Enemy Types[/h2]

[h3]Termitoid[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/8c2fd0bb3bdcdaaf88846bff52c3bc6e29bf5721.gif[/img]

With lightning-fast reflexes and a trusty wrench as their weapon of choice, Termitoid is a formidable opponent that will keep you on your toes.

[h3]Alatoid[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/b229f5b4673b0f3f4285e36e6920fac8afce4448.gif[/img]

With a powerful jetpack that allows for unparalleled mobility, Alatoid rains down electric bolts on unsuspecting agents from above.

[h3]Pincer[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/8ec456a3f99eb0cb38af3d4194bc978279febca5.gif[/img]

This cunning enemy is able to steal C-Balls scattered throughout the map, granting them special abilities that make them an unstoppable force. 

Find new dangerous foes to conquer in the Interport area, with an exciting range of new enemies now available in the game.

[h2]New Boss Encounter[/h2]

[i]"You are not…
 … FREE …
 … from entropy."[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/75714b8711d247f8dad6b4c19cc7c2544889f18a.gif[/img]

[h2]Implants Leveling[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/4c3677dd9acd1266b144d7b38cd939d4160981e5.gif[/img]

Now rather than select a new implant each time, you’ll also get the option of leveling up any implant with an active effect. Each implant can be improved up to [b]three[/b] times, and while the levels of your implants won’t carry over between runs, this new option will no doubt improve how much you get to customize your build. No more ending up with a pile of unused mods in your backpack!

[h2]Implants Rarity[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/8903e8556412cef848d13f192eee3070a3cb0d7e.png[/img]

Now that Deadlink has more implants than before, we'll be splitting them by rarity into three types. Implants will now come in [b]Common[/b], [b]Rare[/b], or [b]Legendary[/b] rarity. It will affect the rate at which they show up on your reward screen:
[list]
[*] 🟩 [b]70%[/b] for Common
[*] 🟦 [b]25%[/b] for Rare
[*] 🟨 [b]5%[/b] for Legendary
[/list]Don’t like the colors in the UI? Think an implant’s not good enough for Legendary? Let us know, and let’s define the rarity system together.

[h2]Challenge Rooms[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/af6c03587bd6f313e8ee16b07df8e9d426f8cba1.gif[/img]

Yes, we know they are all challenging, but let’s talk specifically about challenge rooms. Until now, there was only one type of challenge encountered per biome. But with this update, [b]four more[/b] unique encounters have been added – two for each of the corporations you know and bust. Challenge rooms will also contain new [b]Elite[/b] enemies – stronger versions of loyal corporate servants you’ve encountered. They come with unique looks and a more lethal skillset to set them apart from their peers. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/8ea118757331e2681177dfe450268d7eeeaf629f.gif[/img]

Be sure to report the results and impressions from your encounters!

[h2]Base Stat Changes For Combat Shells[/h2]

To further emphasize the uniqueness of each class and make them even more distinct, we have changed some of the base stats for each available class.

[b]Soldier[/b]
[list]
[*] HP: [b]50 ➡️ 40[/b]
[*] Shield: [b]50 ➡️ 60[/b]
[*] Melee damage: [b]30 ➡️ 40[/b]
[/list]
[b]Hunter[/b]
[list]
[*] Movement speed: [b]700 ➡️ 770[/b]
[*] Ledge grab speed:  [b]550 ➡️ 850[/b]
[/list]
[b]Engineer [/b]
[list]
[*] HP: [b]50 ➡️ 70[/b]
[*] Shield: [b]50 ➡️ 40[/b]
[*] Dash cooldown: [b]1.55s ➡️ 1.15s[/b]
[*] Pickup radius: [b]600 ➡️ 800[/b]
[*] Grenade damage: [b]50 ➡️ 65[/b]
[/list]
[h2]📢 Elemental Damage Modifiers v1.5[/h2]

Thanks to changes to the [b]Elemental Damage Modifiers[/b], they should now feel more distinct from each other (and match the in-game descriptions 🙂).

[b]🔥 Fire Damage[/b]
[list]
[*] Deals extra damage to enemy [b]HP[/b]
[*] Slightly boosts damage to enemy [b]Armor[/b]
[*] Slightly boosts damage to [b]Robotic[/b] enemies
[/list]
[b]☢️ Corrosive Damage[/b]
[list]
[*] Deals extra damage to enemy [b]Armor[/b]
[*] Slightly boosts damage to enemy [b]HP[/b]
[*] Slightly boosts damage to [b]Robotic[/b] enemies
[/list]
[b]⚡Electric Damage[/b]
[list]
[*] Deals extra damage to [b]Robotic[/b] enemies
[*] Slightly boosts damage to enemy [b]HP[/b]
[*] Slightly boosts damage to enemy [b]Armor[/b]
[/list]
[b]Elemental Damage[/b] has been adjusted so that you can still “brute force” your way through by stacking just one element. 

With these changes, it is slightly less optimal to shove all [b]Elemental Mods[/b] into your [b]Primary Weapon[/b] than before. So choose wisely, and adapt to your surroundings!

[h2]Other Changes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Changed the number of combat arenas per biome for the target run-time consistency
[*] 📢 The Translocator, Rappel, and ledge grab will now be considered an in-air movement
[*] Removed horizontal recoil from Gauss Rifle
[*] More reliable controller and Steam Deck support
[*] 📢 Improved visibility of enemies’ weak spots
[*] 📢 Added more customizable video settings
[*] 📢 Bosses no longer see Hunter during his invisibility
[*] Fixed rockets stuck in the air during the Torantula battle
[*] Using Wormlink on a C-Ball will refill all ammo and grant infinite ammo for a duration
[*] Added new Engineer Shell Upgrade - [b]Surge Emitter[/b]
[*] Multiple bug fixes and stability improvements
[/list]
[h1]Dev Note[/h1]

[h2]📢 Heavy Weapons[/h2]

[quote][i]“man heavy weapon door needs to go”[/i]
-- Deadlink’s Discord Wisdom
[/quote]
We heard you, agents! The Heavy Weapon doors may expand variety, but you’ve been beating runs more effectively by never changing your secondary weapon. This leads to you avoiding the Heavy Weapon doors at all.

Hello, agent. Ready to meet the Wizard?

This small update brings to you one of the big talents employed by CSA. None other than the brilliant hacker who helped put together the Engineer class shell. In fact, you’ll be seeing her in the HUB after you unlock it!

In short, here’s what’s packed into this update:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/8af2dad1c4631ce5702a97407f19109f403a7a99.png[/img]

CSA’s newly recruited intelligence expert, a former cyberthief and hacker. Originating from South America, traces of her activities were recorded in a dozen countries, but it can only be speculated how long she has been in the business. Working as a cybersecurity specialist and blackhat for hire, she offered services to high-profile cartels, gangs and corrupt officials. Stealing sensitive data and using it for extorsion, she made herself a small fortune, most of which was spent on a full body prosthesis and an optogenetic brain interface, allowing her to connect to the net at speeds unattainable for most.

The full extent of her “achievements” is unknown due to multiple alias, MO and personality changes, but the times she stepped on the toes of the US intelligence community has proven too many. She was put on Interpol’s notice list, wanted in the States by cyberpolice. Captured 3 years ago, she was placed in complete digital isolation, facing multiple life sentences for the few crimes she could be proven to have committed.

Desperate to reconnect, she offered the US government a deal: her absolute loyalty and ongoing services for dropping her charges and a chance to start another in her long list of new lives. Aware of the possible security risk, the CIA and NSA ghosted her on the offer. Only one man was crazy or brilliant enough to take her up on the offer. Director Thomas Crusher sees her as an important piece needed for his agency’s success.

notes.title: Crisis Levels Update + Patch Notes
notes.content:
Done blowing up everything in your sight on your run? Good! Now, do you have what it takes to do it on a higher tier?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/bc0cd8c9116777ac7e1313553b01b6523bb2238a.jpg[/img]

With the introduction of Crisis Levels you get to up the difficulty of your run. Provided you've already cleared the preceding Crisis Level of course. On each run you will have three levels to choose from, each progressively giving your Combat Shell more of a stress test.

More enemies will be called in to stand in your way. They'll be able to take more punishment while dishing out more to you as well. Your own shield capacity, mark duration and ammo received from drops will suffer on higher Crisis Level.

Of course all this high risk comes with high rewards back at HQ! Besting the corps at a higher Crisis Level will allow you to unlock more powerful HUB upgrades. Clearing both levels, including defeating both bosses, at maximum Crisis Level will earn you a special weapon skin to flaunt your victory! Shotgun skin for the Soldier and Peacekeeper skin for the Hunter. 

Think you've had enough practice on the default difficulty? Then raise that Crisis Level and prove you've mastered the use of your Combat Shell!


[h1][b]Deadlink Patch Notes[/b][/h1]

[u]2022-11-07[/u]

"📢" [i]marks the changes suggested by the Deadlink community[/i]


[h2]New Features[/h2]
[list]
[*] Crisis Levels with three difficulty tiers (described in the next section)
[*] 📢 Fall animations and fall damage added to enemies
[*] 📢 Added option to display run info on HUD (Crisis Level and the number of areas completed)
[*] New VO was added to the Phoenix Apex boss
[*] New Soldier’s Shell Upgrade: [i]If an enemy is killed within 2 seconds of being hooked, the cooldown for the GripWire Rappel is reset.[/i]
[/list]

[h2]Bugfixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] HUB was heavily optimized in case of CPU and GPU consumption
[*] Fixed a bug that prevented launching the game while the VR headset was connected to the PC
[*] Fixed the aspect ratio issue after watching cutscenes on ultrawide resolutions
[*] Fixed the highest damage telemetry stat that often was equal to 0
[*] Fixed the sometimes-invisible container on the Torantula boss arena
[*] Fixed annoying laser sound on one of the Watts-Rucker arenas
[*] Fixed Mothership and Hound data displayed in Codex and after being killed by these units
[*] Fix the issue with incorrect ammo stacking when using Electrolaser
[*] Fixed the wrong name of the Combat Shell during the tutorial
[*] Fixed a bug that resulted in detaching the camera from the FPS view
[*] Fixed the gamepad usage in HUB
[*] Fixed the footstep sounds that sometimes persisted after killing an enemy
[*] Fixed the bug that could cause a player to kill himself with a shock damage
[*] Lots of arenas’ collision and minor fixes
[/list]
[h2]Tweaks[/h2]

[h3]General[/h3]
[list]
[*] 📢 Added max grenades HUD notification
[*] 📢 Changed tutorial popups to be closed with the ESC button
[*] Tank enemy; weak spots added, HP increase x2
[*] Rikishi enemy; weak spot added, HP increase x1.5
[*] Reduce teleport frequency of Geisha enemy
[*] Hound enemy; projectile explosion improvements - no longer obscures player vision
[*] Neuralboosts:
     ○ Weapon Damage removed
     ○ Headshot Damage removed
     ○ Primary Weapon Damage lowered to 10% from 20%
     ○ Secondary Weapon Damage lowered to 10% from 20%
[*] Tweaks to enemies’ movement and path selection. Many collision issues were resolved
[/list]
[h3]Soldier [/h3]

[b]Shotgun[/b]
[list]
[*] 📢 Improved initial pellet distribution. Targets very close to the player will be easier to hit
[*] Improved shotgun pellet collision logic. This should provide better consistency at close to mid-range shots
[/list]
[h3]Hunter[/h3]

[b]Peacekeeper[/b]
[list]
[*] Lowered recoil recovery speed, recoil halftime decay increased from 0.14 to 0.24
[*] Base damage reduced to 50
[*] The headshot damage multiplier lowered from 1.75 to 1.5
[*] 📢 Headshot mod: headshot bonus damage increased from 50% to 300%
[/list]
[b]ARC[/b]
[list]
[*] 📢 Decreased charge-up time for all ARC mods
[*] Increased fire rate of Matter Converter
[*] ARC mod Particle Accelerator will zoom in and slightly slow down time while charging
[*] ARC mod Particle Accelerator damage increased from 120 to 150
[/list]
[b]Translocator[/b]
[list]
[*] 📢 Improved post-swap enemy positioning (enemies will be placed at the exact player’s location instead of slightly above)
[/list]
[b]Decoy[/b]
[list]
[*] Explosion now marks enemies and penetrates armor
[*] Lifetime reduced from 10s to 5s
[*] Enemy melee damage instantly activates the decoy explosion
[*] Explosive Decoy mod: 
[*] The Skill Power multiplier increased from 1 to 3
[/list]


[h2]Crisis Levels[/h2]

🗨️ [b]Dev comment: [/b]First of all, please keep in mind that this is the first iteration of the difficulty tiers system, and we plan to build upon it based on your feedback.

In the current state, the difficulty comes from higher enemy stats (HP, attack power) and higher enemy numbers and composition (fights will last longer), and also lowering player stats (mark duration, shields dropped from enemies, and ammo dropped by anchors). We know it doesn't really sound exciting, but we have to do this so that the game can keep up with your HUB upgrades (flat dmg/hp/shield boosts).

To incorporate difficulty tiers more into the game, we've connected them with HUB upgrade tiers, so you will have to beat the game on the higher difficulty in order to unlock more powerful HUB upgrades.

Higher difficulty tiers also offer better rewards (XP and Tokens) to make it worth your time. You'll also get something special for beating the game on (currently) the highest difficulty.

As we move forward, we will experiment with adding more variety to the difficulty tiers by implementing new abilities for enemies, handcrafting encounters for maximum pressure, and adjusting HUB upgrades.


[h2]Hunter, Neuralboosts, and Bonus Damage calculation[/h2]

🗨️ [b]Dev comment:[/b] Hunter is still very much overpowered; to be more precise - Peacekeeper is still very much overpowered. It has high ammo capacity, no fire rate (shoots as fast as you can click), very low recoil, extremely low reload speed, and is good at both close and mid-range. No cons. It's just too good to be a primary weapon, really. Most of you (and us) don't even use ARC at all in order to beat the game. So we've looked closely into Peacekeeper progression, and we've made some changes based on our findings:

[h3]Identity Crisis[/h3]

Peacekeeper was supposed to be a precision-based weapon, but it turns out it can be even more effective by unloading the whole clip into the enemy body. At the same time, we'd like to keep the feeling of fanning the hammer into tankier enemies.

So we've decided to keep Peacekeeper as a "ratatat machine" by default, with an option to turn it into slow firing, head-popping cannon using weapon mods.

[h3]3 Neuralboosts is All It Takes[/h3]

We noticed that it took very little effort to turn the Peacekeeper into the best weapon in the game.

When choosing a Neuralboost, you had too many options to buff Peacekeeper damage, and it could get out of control quickly. Primary Weapon Damage, Weapon Damage, Crit Damage, Headshot Damage + Elemental Damage boost (if you had elemental weapon mod). You would start the game and deal 150 headshot damage during the first two arenas. In some scenarios, just after 3 arenas, you bring this damage up to 600. Combine that with an unlimited fire rate, and you've no reason to pick any other upgrade for the rest of your run. That's why we’ve removed the Headshot damage boost and decreased primary/secondary weapon boosts.

[h3]Multiplication Goes Brrrrrrrrrrrr[/h3]

The other thing connected to Neuralboosts is the overall damage calculation. All damage boosts were multiplicative; for example, you have a fire damage mod on your Peacekeeper, and you're about to deal 100 damage to a marked target. You have a 20% damage boost to marked enemies and a 50% fire damage boost. The system would multiply everything like: 100 * 1.2 * 1.5 = 180. Because you had multiple sources of damage boosts, this would cause your damage to skyrocket later during the run when you would gather dozens of different multipliers.

We've decided to make all damage boosts additive, so in the same scenario, you would do 100 * (1 + 0.2 + 0.5) = 170 damage. This will help keep player damage in line with increasing game difficulty and eliminate the issue of one-shotting everything deeper into the run. You can still create a pretty OP build by combining Shell Upgrades, Implants, and Neuralboosts.

All in all, Hunter's weapons are now more balanced, and while you can still stick to the Peacekeeper on most occasions, it will be more difficult to get it to the state of a godlike weapon and maybe convince you to use ARC more often.


[h2]Fall Damage[/h2]
🗨️ [b]Dev comment:[/b] This was an interesting suggestion from the community and turned out to be a fun little gimmick. Falling enemies will take damage based on traveled distance and their max HP.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/d7ee0fb02ef012f4e6652a813e982ecc9743e461.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/55a5e41c85b8d66bfe1080e778b4bc11c3122cb2.gif[/img]

[h2]Community Q&A[/h2]

[b]"Where co-op?"[/b]

Deadlink is a single-player experience, and it will stay that way. We have no plans to add any form of multiplayer.

[b]"Where melee class?"[/b]

Deadlink is a first-person shooter - not a first-person slasher. Gunplay is at its core, and we've put a lot of effort into making shooting a great experience. While we probably could make a pure melee class, we don't think we could bring it to the level of polish that guns have. At least not in a reasonable timeframe.

Having a melee class would also mean that we have to redesign some of the game's core mechanics - for example, the Torantula boss fight. Good luck slicing this bad boy up with a katana.

While we have planned a class that will be encouraged to stay close to the enemies, it will not be a pure melee class.

There's still a lot we can and want to do regarding gunplay, and we can't wait to share more details when the time is right.

notes.title: Hotfix - October 2022
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41652932/3d5ecc3993eb581c8a0f23639a791d8a8387a2b6.png[/img]

Our first patch is here! It mainly contains balance tweaks to Hunter and some bug fixes. We've been overwhelmed by the positive reception of Deadlink and can't wait to push new content out. Thank you for your feedback, and keep it coming! 🔥

[h1]Hunter[/h1] 
[b]💬 Dev comment:[/b] Reading user feedback and analyzing your gameplay allowed us to realize how unbalanced two combat shells are. While we think Soldier is in a good place, Hunter needs some attention. This is probably the first round of Hunter nerfs, but we want to take it easy and get to the sweet spot of rewarding but challenging gameplay.

[h2]ARC[/h2]
[list]
[*] ARC gun will no longer stun enemies
[*] ARC gun will stagger enemies hit
[/list]
[b]💬 Dev comment:[/b] ARC gun stun was straight-out overpowered as you could just stand there and unload on a bunch of heavy enemies - that's not the gameplay we want to promote with Hunter. We want to address stun mechanics in the future by implementing diminishing returns (the more you stun enemies, the more resistant they are to it), but for now, we will just remove stun from the ARC gun and replace it with a stagger. Stun locking was just OP and too easy to execute.

[h2]Decoy[/h2]
[list]
[*] Decoy HP reduced from 50 to 25
[*] Decoy lifetime reduced from 10 to 5 seconds
[*] Fixed a bug where some enemies wouldn't do damage to Decoy
[/list]
[b]💬 Dev comment:[/b] In our opinion decoy/Vanish combo is the most overpowered and least fun skill to use - you just push the button and get out of any trouble. While it's fun to watch enemies get distracted and get some breathing room, we think 10 seconds duration is just too generous.

[h1]New Features[/h1]
[list]
[*] Added Crash Reporter
[*] Added 1 new combat arena to the Tora biome
[/list]
[h3]Gathering pickups after arena bug[/h3]
Did you know that after the combat arena is completed, we vacuum all pickups (shields, grenades, credits, etc) from the entire map so that you don't have to frantically run around and try to pick them up?
Well, we've detected a bug where players would receive more shields than they should. This resulted in leaving almost every arena with a full shield (even if no shield was lying around). We believe this bug was the main reason players could beat the game so fast, even without any HUB upgrades. This might give you the false impression that the game is too easy right from the get-go. It has been fixed, and we hope that player accountability will be where it should be from the beginning. 

[h1]Other Fixes[/h1]
[list]
[*] fixed the issue with the broken camera after Hunter's swap
[*] fixed lack of collision at some doors that resulted in the player falling out of a map
[*] fixes lore typos
[*] fixed save & exit functionality that resulted in a wrong data loaded
[*] fixed heal after arena HUB upgrade that wasn't working on some conditions
[*] fixed DoT effects not being affected by elemental damage multiplier
[*] fixed arena rewards sound that would loop indefinitely after opening the menu
[*] fixed shop items refresh after selling implants
[*] fixed broken game state when abandoning the run after killing a boss
[*] lots of optimization fixes
[/list]
Our next patch will introduce difficulty tiers and hopefully create a challenge for some of you :)

notes.title: Deadlink FAQ
notes.content:
[b]What is Deadlink?[/b]
Deadlink is a cyberpunk FPS with roguelite elements, which means you shoot, you die, you upgrade your weapons and go shooting again, but with enhanced abilities!

[b]Who is developing Deadlink?[/b]
Deadlink is created by Gruby Entertainment, a studio founded by ex-developers from People Can Fly, the team who worked previously on Outriders. Deadlink is published by Super.com.

[b]Will the game be localised into other languages?[/b]
Right now we’re focusing on the abovementioned languages. Other localizations might be added at later stages of development.

[b]Is there a roadmap for the game?[/b]
There isn’t one yet, but we are planning to share it soon, once our game launches in Early Access!

[b]What are the recommended specs for Deadlink?[/b]
[b]CPU[/b] - AMD Ryzen™ 5 2600 (Intel i7-4770)
[b]GPU[/b] - AMD Radeon™ RX 590 or NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1060 6GB
[b]Mem[/b] - 16 GB RAM
[b]OS[/b] - Windows 10 64-bit
[b]Storage[/b] - 15 GB available space

[b]What are the minimum specs for Deadlink?[/b]
[b]CPU[/b] - AMD FX-8350 or Intel i5-3570
[b]GPU[/b] - AMD Radeon™ HD 7970 or NVIDIA GeForce GTX 680 2 GB
[b]Mem[/b] - 6 GB RAM
[b]OS[/b] - Windows 10 64-bit
[b]Storage[/b] - 15 GB available space

[b]Will there be controller support?[/b]
Yes! There will be full controller support. 

[b]Where can I view all the updates?[/b]
Updates will be posted on our social media profiles, [url=https://bit.ly/discord_deadlink]Deadlink Discord server[/url] and on our [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1676130]Steam Community Page[/url].

[b]Will the game be coming out on platforms other than Steam?[/b]

[b]How do I join the Deadlink Community?[/b]
